body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\), estimated by the raw \(\widehat\tau\).  This equality is identified under event transport.  The sharp conditional-risk rate \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and the uniformly honest expected-length rate \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\) hold over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), which imposes the two stated full-design centering restrictions.  The donor component remains conditional on the assumed two-sided local modulus, and no sequential-overlap or other anti-clustering condition is imposed.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on \(E_0\), each cohort contributes \(T\) exactly observed pre-event proxy paths with one-time densities bounded above and away from zero.  Their calendar process is geometrically beta mixing; this permits logarithmic blocks of repeated local states and therefore entails the uniform spacing scale \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{1/d}\).
sampling_model.units: At each pre-event path, cohort \(s\) supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded untreated wealth blocks, and the event date supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded treated wealth levels; event units need not be identically distributed.
sampling_model.treatment: The event occurs at \(t=0\). Consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and the maintained cross-date cohort-average event-transport equality identify the untreated finite-cohort event mean from the historical path regression.
sampling_model.overlap: The realized event path lies in an interior positive-probability region and every historical design density is bounded below there.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample of size \(N\) estimates only the event query under a full uniformly elliptic covariance and a fourth-moment envelope; historical training coordinates are exact.  Fixed-fold projected donor means feed a log-adjusted local-polynomial fit selected by normalized Gram shape.  The interval uses the full-data smoothing weights, separate historical and event cluster-level Hoeffding radii, an exact Holder--Taylor allowance, and a donor-modulus allowance, with \([-B,B]\) fallback on the declared bad sample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper derives identification and asymptotic-bias conditions for financial event-study estimators and explains that buy-and-hold comparisons require volatility matching.
The Holder repeated-measurement prediction rate has sparse order \((nm)^{-2s/(2s+d)}\) and dense order \(n^{-1}\), up to the stated logarithmic qualifications.
A local-polynomial Lepski procedure adapts pointwise to local design mass and local Holder smoothness under observed random design.
Theorem 1 expands local-linear regression with a generated covariate attached to every training observation through smoothed first-stage errors.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 establish deconvolution rates when latent training coordinates have replicated classical measurement error.
Theorems 7--8 evaluate a rate-optimal local-polynomial regression estimator at a sample-split estimated strongly convex minimizer.
The dependent-data theorem uses large-block--small-block coupling for conditional approximation of synthetic-control prediction error.
Spline and wavelet series estimators attain optimal uniform rates and functional normality under beta mixing and weak moments.
Ordered moduli characterize optimal confidence procedures for linear functionals over convex regression classes in a fixed Gaussian experiment.
The many-period--many-control result gives conditions for synthetic-control factor-loading recovery under imperfect pre-treatment fit.
The proximal synthetic-control theorems identify treatment effects by using excluded control outcomes as predetermined proxies.

body.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path.  Consistency and a maintained cohort-average event-transport restriction identify it through historical conditional-mean surfaces, and the raw generated-center local-polynomial estimator is exactly an event coefficient in a foldwise weighted panel regression.  Over the explicitly restricted full-design-centered class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), matching lower and upper bounds give conditional mean-squared-error rate \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and uniformly honest expected-length rate \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  Geometric beta mixing and marginal density alone yield the unavoidable spacing term \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\); a rare-block witness rules out the iid spacing rate uniformly without an additional anti-clustering condition.  The feasible full-data interval combines separate bounded cluster-level Hoeffding radii, an exact Holder--Taylor allowance, and a fourth-moment donor-modulus allowance.  The donor channel saturates at \(N^{-1}\) in mean squared error when \(\lambda>1\), conditional on the assumed two-sided local modulus.

project_justification.gap: Causal financial event-study theory mainly treats linear return contrasts; repeated-measurement regression fixes the query; generated-regressor theory typically moves training coordinates; and synthetic-control inference does not deliver a generated-event-proxy minimax frontier for compounded wealth under arbitrary relative growth.
project_justification.niche: The panel architecture here observes historical proxy paths exactly, replicates untreated wealth blocks at each calendar window, and estimates only the event-date query from an independent donor sample.  It separates unit replication, calendar path coverage, and generated-center uncertainty without a classical measurement-error inverse problem.
project_justification.fill: The project proves finite-cohort causal identification under explicit event transport, an exact weighted-panel coefficient representation, and matching risk and honest-length frontiers over the transparent full-design-centered subclass.  A normalized Gram-shape selector, full-data cluster-level Hoeffding calibration, exact Taylor allowance, covariance-standardized donor control, and four channelwise causal-panel witnesses establish the result without sequential overlap or an upper local-mass condition.

body.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the causal financial-panel setup and show why volatility mismatch makes buy-and-hold effects harder than linear cumulative returns; their result informs the maintained event-transport identification layer rather than serving as a theorem-level target. Yan, Yao, and Zhou (2023, revised 2025) provide repeated-measurement Holder rates and a sparse-to-dense decomposition, while Gaiffas (2007) provides the pointwise random-design local-mass template. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) analyze generated coordinates attached to every training observation; Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) analyze replicated classical coordinate error requiring deconvolution. Those observation experiments inform the sigma-field distinction here. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closest conditional synthetic-control uncertainty decomposition and beta-mixing block coupling. Chen and Christensen (2015) provide weak-dependence Gram-matrix control for higher-order sieve regression. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) provide the ordered-modulus language for honest expected length. Ferman (2021) supplies the many-period--many-control motivation for retaining arbitrary relative growth. Shi et al. (2026) identify synthetic controls through predetermined donor proxies but do not study generated-proxy minimax behavior.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Causal identification remains conditional on the maintained event-transport equality.  The risk and honest-length theorems additionally use the two explicit strong full-design strict-exogeneity and historical-centering restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\); neither follows from contemporaneous regression centering or conditional cross-unit independence.  The two-sided local modulus is assumed rather than derived over the whole Holder ball, so flat surfaces are outside the donor lower-bound subclass.  The results keep \(S\) and \(p(H+1)\) fixed and do not provide smoothness adaptation or sharp constants.
body.honest_scope: The proved contribution consists of the event-transport identification formula, exact raw-estimator FWL identity, normalized-shape local-polynomial control, log-adjusted geometric-mixing selector bound, positive-affinity rare-block spacing obstruction, four channelwise causal-panel embeddings, and matching conditional risk and uniformly honest expected-length frontiers over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).  No sequential-overlap, dense-local-site, upper-local-mass, event conditional-variance, studentization, or temporal-within-unit independence condition is added.  The same-class logarithmic spacing term is unavoidable under the maintained assumptions.  The iid rate is only a stricter-design comparator.  The donor converse is conditional on the two-sided local modulus, and all causal interpretation remains conditional on event transport.
body.interpretation: The active risk is, up to fixed constants, the maximum of treated-cohort averaging noise, log-adjusted calendar spacing, and generated-donor uncertainty; the replicated-smoothing term is retained for bookkeeping but cannot be uniquely active.  The oracle region has donor error asymptotically smaller than the other active terms, the generated-proxy region has it larger, and the boundary equates \(N^{-\kappa}\) with their maximum.  The iid spacing expression \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) applies only under independent design, or under a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition that delivers it.
